Skill.Explanation: "Runesmithing is used for crafting magical runes, and to harness magic to reawaken or deactivate runes forged by others. It is a difficult, exacting Skill, that requires formidable concentration, with none of the immediate flashy effects of conventional spellcraft. Much of the process is conducted by gut instinct, and subconscious attunement with magical forces. This distinguishes the Skill from Lore (Runes): any Dwarf can learn runelore if given the chance, but only a few have the gift to transmute the Winds of Magic into physical form."

Talent.Description: "Master Rune Magic (Protection Runes and Weapon Runes)"

Specie.Explanation: "All that is most glorious about the Everlasting Realm can be found in the Dwarf capital of Karaz-a-Karak. Adventurers from the Everpeak act as self-appointed representatives of the High King himself, binding themselves to his vow to right every wrong in the Great Book of Grudges."

"The home of the Dwarf navy is based in the Border Princes, a rare beacon of stability amongst lawless Human kingdoms. Its people trade extensively with the neighbouring principalities, and are generally more welcoming and curious about the outside world."

"The weapon-smithies of Karak Azul have become a dark and joyless place since the kidnapping of King Kazador's kin by the Orc warlord Gorfang Rotgut. A king's ransom has been promised to the adventurers that return the captured kin from Black Crag, and slay the monster Gorfang."

"Karak Eight Peaks is an active warzone, as King Belegar's kin fight an endless siege to liberate the occupied hold. Clansfolk are rarely permitted to leave the front, but adventurous Dwarfs may be dispatched abroad to find weapons, allies, or information that can help wage the war at home."

"The Slayer's Keep is the centre of worship for Grimnir, the Dwarf god of war. Many warriors live and die here, battling to control the critical Peak Pass connecting the Old World to the far east. For others, it is just as the first step of their journey, to seek glorious combat wherever it is found."

"Zhufbar is the main hub of Dwarf industry, and the centre of the Engineering Guild. The Karak is always at the forefront of technical innovation, with greater acceptance of new ideas than is found in other holds. Field tests of new inventions often carry its inhabitants far from home."

"Much travel through the Black Mountains is conducted overland, and adventurous Dwarfs in the region are as comfortable scrabbling up mountainsides as delving into Goblin tunnels. Foremost amongst this range is Karak Hirn, the Hornhold, which exploits the natural acoustics of their surrounding canyons to signal the outside world."

"The Vaults were the first ranges settled by Dwarfs outside the World's Edge Mountains, with Karak Izor its centre of defence. Whilst most Dwarfs have abandoned the subterranean tunnels of the Karaz Ankor as unsafe, the Dwarfs of Karak Izor labour underground extensively, constructing their own Underway."

"The holds of the Grey Mountains were never prosperous, and their inhabitants learned long ago how to persist in lean times. Many have abandoned their holds to seek opportunity elsewhere. In Karak Norn, distrust of the Wood Elves in Athel Loren rarely abates, and missions to surveil the devious Elves are often led astray."

"The Dwarfs of the frozen north are hearty and independent. After centuries of isolation, they are keen to explore the wider world, by exercising the naval expertise they gleaned from cultural exchange with Human tribes. Even by Dwarf standards, their drinking binges are legendary."

"The reign of Sigmar, Wars of the Vampire Counts, and Great War Against Chaos were all succeeded by waves of Dwarfen expatriation in the Empire. Their numbers are periodically swelled by Karak exiles, and refugees from fallen holds. Though often disparaged by their mountaintop cousins, Imperial Dwarfs emulate both the traditional customs of Karaz Ankor, and the manling tendency to seek glory through adventure."

Talent.Explanation: "Choose a culture or faction that is the target of your Ancestral Grudge (e.g. Orcs, Goblins, Skaven, Trolls, Daemons of Khorne). Enter them into your Book of Grudges as the target of your vengeance. You bear this group a Blood Grudge that can never be satisfied. However, every time you win a significant victory against this group (destroying their works, taking back something stolen, killing many of their kind) you gain 50 XP. Each time you purchase this Talent, you gain an Ancestral Grudge against a different faction. At the GM's discretion, declaring vengeance against a smaller sub-faction can award more XP: 75 XP per victory against a specific Goblin tribe, 100 XP per victory against a specific Human family line."
"When you win an opposed Test to activate the Pummel Quality, you inflict an additional Stunned Condition for each level of Bludgeoner."

"When you activate the Hack Quality as part of an attack, you inflict +1 additional Damage on struck armour or shields for each level of Demolisher. In addition, when attacking an enemy in cover with a weapon that has the Hack Quality, hard cover counts as medium cover, medium cover counts as soft cover, and soft cover provides no protection at all."
Talent.Test: "Melee when breaking inanimate objects using a Hack weapon"

Talent.Explanation: "When you fire a weapon with the Blackpowder Quality, targeted enemies who fail their Cool Test gain an additional Broken Condition for each level of Dragon Belcher."
"When you are in soft cover, attacks against you are Hard (-20) instead of Difficult (-10). When you are in medium cover, attacks against you are Very Hard (-30) instead of Hard (-20)."

"When you are Engaged, any melee weapons wielded by yourself or an ally within Willpower Bonus yards gain the Penetrating Quality. If an affected weapon is already Penetrating, its attacks now ignore 1 additional point of non-metal armour."

"When you gain the Unconscious Condition, you can interrupt the Turn order to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action, before you are taken out of action. When you gain the Stunned Condition, you can spend a Fortune point to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action. You take your next Turn as usual, which means you cannot take an Action if you are still Stunned."

"When you inflict a Critical Hit with a Crossbow weapon, you may increase your roll on the Critical Hit table by +10 for each level of Harpooner, to a maximum of 00. In addition, Crossbow bolts lodged into the target's body due to the Impale Quality reduce the target's Movement by 1 per bolt, to a minimum of 1."

"Any enemy attacks against an ally within 2 yards of you suffer a -10 modifier for each level of Kingsguard. This Talent does not apply to attacks against yourself, nor does it apply if you are currently suffering from a Condition."

"You gain +10 Strength and Toughness after consuming an alcoholic drink. This provides an immediate bonus to your Consume Alcohol Test for consuming the drink, and the benefit continues to apply whether you succeed or fail on that Test. You retain this bonus until an hour has passed since your last alcoholic drink; drinking again can prolong the effect, but does not increase your Characteristic bonuses beyond +10."

"When recalling significant events you were involved in previously in the campaign, you can perfectly remember the time, date, location, and visible faces of all individuals present, and exactly what those present pledged to say or do. If recalling a significant event you witnessed before the campaign began, you may need to take an Intelligence Test to remember details, with a difficulty set by the intervening time: Easy (+40) for events mere months ago, Hard (-20) for events a century ago."
"You can Reverse any Test you are obliged to make as part of a magic spell's effects, as well as Tests to dispel magic with Magic Resistance."

"Choose a master rune from pages 127-131. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a master rune from the specified lists. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen master rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new master rune you can craft. The first time you acquire this Talent, you also learn all three Doom Runes (page 132)."
"You do not suffer the -20 penalty on Ranged attacks when using the Flight Creature Trait."
Talent.Test: "Sail (Skycraft) Tests to fly fast and dangerous"

Talent.Explanation: "Choose a rune from pages 127-131. You cannot select a master rune. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a rune from the specified lists. If it specifies a specific rune (e.g. the Rune of Stone), you must choose that specific rune. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new rune you can craft."
"When using an Explosive weapon with the Blast Quality, increase its Rating by +1 for each level of Short Fuse."
"When you apply penalties due to suffering from the Fatigued Condition, you may ignore 1 instance of the Fatigued Condition, +1 additional Fatigued Condition for each level of Tireless."

"You do not suffer penalties for attacking whilst you have the Prone Condition, or are otherwise beneath your target. Enemies do not get a bonus to attack you whilst you have the Prone Condition. You gain an additional +20 to hit Surprised enemies, when you are emerging from a tunnel, pit, or other hidden position below them."

"As an Action, you can spend 1 Fortune to make a Melee attack against all creatures Engaged with you. The GM chooses one enemy to Oppose this Test. If your attack succeeds, you inflict the same Damage to the same Hit Location against all Engaged creatures, calculated as normal. Do not apply Criticals on Whirlwind of Death attacks, though Critical Wounds are inflicted on enemies reduced to 0 Wounds as normal. You cannot activate any other special attack options as part of a Whirlwind of Death. However, a Character with Dual Wielder wielding two weapons as part of a Whirlwind of Death may Reverse their Melee attack Test."

Career.Explanation: "You prepare alcoholic drinks of such strength and quality that no Dwarf can fail to appreciate them."
"You are a professional bodyguard and elite warrior, enjoying pride of place in any Dwarfen army."

Item.name: Runic Hammer or Runic Battle Standard

Career.Explanation: "You are a specialist tunnel fighter, armoured in nigh-indestructible gromril to endure the horrors of the sunless underworld."
"You are a nomadic, overland traveller, living off the land, and keeping a wary eye on the enemies of your people."
"You are the leader of a Dwarf Clan, or soon to inherit the position."
"You lionise the great warrior ancestors of your people, encouraging younger Dwarfs to follow their example."
"You preserve and restore the oldest examples of Dwarfen craftsmanship to honour the master-builders who preceded you."
"You lead and protect your kin as the Ancestor Gods expect - with healing balms, stirring words, and good ale."
"You are a diligent record keeper, inscribing essential information in stone so it is preserved until long after your death."
"You are a practitioner of runic magic, binding the Winds of Magic into physical objects through ritual craftsmanship."

"Guild Engineers train not just to assemble war machines but to accompany them into battle, and supervise the industry of the Karaks between campaigns. Alternate 2nd level of Engineer or Artillerist."

"Gyrocopters and other skycraft are still distrusted by the Guild's elders, but many of the most daring Engineers are experts at maintaining and piloting them. Alternate 3rd level of Engineer, advancing Agility in place of Toughness."

"Those who challenge the Engineers Guild's hidebound conservatism are fated to undergo an elaborate exiling ritual, yet many still practise their calling independently. Alternate 3rd level of Engineer or Artillerist, advancing Fellowship in place of Toughness."
"Reckoners are intermediaries who carry records of outstanding grudges between clans and holds, negotiating settlements on their clients' behalf. Alternate 2nd level of Lawyer."
"Grudgemasters are the ultimate authorities on grudges and proportionate restitution, dictating the wording of grudges for their Kings to inscribe. Alternate 3rd level of Lawyer."

Item.name: Key to the Hall of Remembering

Career.Explanation: "Stoneshapers are a combination of mason, architect and combat engineer, specialising in stone fortifications and famed for anticipating rockfalls. Alternate 2nd level of Artisan, advancing Initiative in place of Fellowship."
"When called to war, the warriors of the Miner's Guild fight as they work, wielding picks and travelling underground to undermine and outmanoeuvre their enemies. Alternate 2nd level of Miner."
"The elite of the mining clans, Lodefinders sniff out valuable deposits and are trusted to drive or operate advanced mining engineering equipment. Alternate 3rd level of Miner."
"Runebearers are long-distance runners who deliver vital messages between holds, specialising in the tunnels of the Underway. Alternate 2nd level of Messenger."
"Experienced Slayers inducted into the Brotherhood of Grimnir by the Doom Priests mark their dedication with runic tattoos of warding. Alternate 2nd level of Slayer."
"Loners even by Slayer standards, Doomseekers fasten axes to themselves with locked chains, hoping to take hundreds of enemies down with them. Alternate 3rd level of Slayer."

"War-mourner was once the title of ancient Dwarf champions, oathsworn to uphold their king's honour on his behalf in battle. Alternate 4th level of Slayer, advancing Fellowship in place of Initiative."

"By long tradition regiments of Dwarfs go to battle carrying axes as their primary weapon, preferring the heft of a solid war axe over the finesse of a sword. Alternate 2nd level of Soldier, advancing Strength in place of Ballistic Skill."
"Crossbows are the traditional Dwarf hunting weapon, and disciplined ranks of Quarrellers have formed the basis of throng firing lines for millennia. Alternate 2nd level of Soldier."

"Dwarf handguns are far more precise and reliable than Imperial counterparts, and the cacophonous roar of a Thunderer's volley is terrifying enough to put survivors to flight. Alternate 2nd level of Soldier or Handgunner."

BonusMalus.Explanation: "A Salvo weapon can be fired a number of times equal to its Rating before it needs to be reloaded. When shooting a Salvo weapon, you can choose to fire a single shot (reducing Salvo by 1), or a batch of missiles (reducing Salvo by the number of shots fired). Each missile fired after the first suffers a cumulative -10 on its Ranged Test. The Reload Rating of a Salvo weapon indicates the SLs required to increase its Salvo by 1. If a Dwarf Salvo weapon Misfires on a roll of 00, the crew suffers a number of hits equal to the weapon's remaining Salvo Rating (minimum 1)."

"For this weapon to operate optimally, it must be crewed by the number of characters equal to its Rating, all with the relevant Ranged skill (e.g. a Crewed (3) weapon requires 3 trained crew to operate efficiently). Only one crewmember can fire the weapon each Round, but additional crew can move or reload the weapon in their Turn. Misfires damage all characters crewing the weapon, to a random hit location instead of the Primary Arm. A Crewed weapon with insufficient crew doubles its Reload Rating. In addition, the weapon gains the Imprecise Flaw if it is short 2 or more crew, and the Dangerous Flaw if it is short 3 or more crew. If this effect would duplicate Flaws the weapon already has, it inflicts -10 on Ranged Tests per duplicated Flaw."
BonusMalus.Short: "needs a crew of (Rating), impaired if short-handed"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "Weapons with the Spread Quality fire an expanding cloud of projectiles which may strike several targets. Depending on the range to the target, weapons with this Quality behave somewhat differently. Point Blank: The shot targets a single individual. Add (Rating) to the weapon's Damage. Short Range to Long Range: The shot targets a single individual, and also the next (Rating) closest visible creatures. No two targets may be more than (Rating) yards apart. Extreme Range: As for Short to Long Range but reduce the weapon's Damage by (Rating)."

Craftsmanship.Explanation: "The weapon inflicts +1 Damage for each Rune of Cleaving."
"Any Critical Wounds inflicted by this weapon may add +20 to rolls on a Critical Wound table for each Rune of Retribution."
"When attacking with this weapon, you may ignore 2 APs of armour per Rune of Cutting on successful hits."

"Whilst this weapon is drawn, you gain the Fear Creature Trait. Your Fear Rating is equal to the number of Runes of Daunting. If you already have a Fear Rating, increase it by +1 for each Rune of Daunting."

"Once drawn, the weapon's blade bursts into flames, providing 20 yards of illumination, and inflicting 1 Ablaze Condition on enemies it inflicts damage upon. A weapon with two or three Runes of Fire can be used to make ranged attacks using Ballistic Skill, with a Range equal to the wielder's Willpower Bonus, and the Blast 4 Quality. This attack deals no Damage, but inflicts 1 Ablaze Condition for each Rune of Fire."

"Whilst wielding this weapon, you gain 1 level of Dual Wielder for each Rune of Fury, which may exceed the Talent usual maximum levels. For purposes of activating Dual Wielder, you may count a weapon bearing the Rune of Fury as two separate weapons, one in each hand, allowing you to attack two targets even if you aren't carrying a second weapon."

"Nominate an enemy you bear a Blood Grudge. For each Grudge Rune, the weapon gains both +10 to hit and +1 Damage on attacks against the target. At the end of the adventure, if your nominated enemy is slain, you may nominate a new target against whom you bear a Blood Grudge."
"When attacking a target of a larger Size than yourself, the weapon inflicts +3 Damage for each Rune of Might."
"Whilst carrying this weapon in combat, you gain +10 Initiative for each Rune of Speed."

"When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to your Melee Skill for each Rune of Striking (the specialisation for the Melee Skill being the same as the Weapon Type of the weapon upon which the rune is inscribed). The bonus only applies to strikes with this weapon."
"Any attacks made by this weapon ignore the target's AP, the target's armour Qualities, and any other benefits provided by the target's armour."

"When this weapon makes a successful attack against an enemy who Opposed with Melee, or makes a successful Melee Test to Oppose an incoming attack, any magic weapon used by your opponent during their Melee Test is destroyed."
"The weapon can be used as a Thrown ranged weapon, with a Range of SB x3. When used on a ranged attack, the weapon gains the Accurate Quality, and returns to your hand after inflicting Damage."
"Any successful attack with this weapon counts as scoring a Critical."

"Choose a specific type of enemy: Daemons, Undead, Dragons, Goblins, Elves, etc. When attacking that target with this weapon, you may Reverse any attack Tests, and Reverse any rolls they make on a Critical Wound table."
"Any failed Melee Tests made with this weapon always count as achieving a success with 0 SL. An attack with this weapon can still fail if the target scores more SLs on their Opposed Test."
"The weapon gains the Fast Quality, except all Tests to defend against the weapon with Melee suffer a -30 penalty (instead of -10)."
"Whilst wearing this armour, if you make a successful Melee attack as part of a Charge, you inflict bonus Damage for each Rune of Impact equal to the APs of your most armoured location."
"Whilst wearing this armour, you increase your Toughness by +10 for each Rune of Fortitude."
"Whilst wearing this armour, you gain +2 Wounds for each Rune of Iron. These Wounds are lost when the armour is removed, which can trigger a Critical Wound for a severely injured Character."
"Whilst wearing this armour, you gain +10 for each Rune of Resistance on Tests to Oppose an incoming Melee attack."

"Whilst wearing this armour, any incoming ranged attacks or spells reduce the Damage they inflict by 2 for each Rune of Shielding. If this reduces Damage inflicted to 0 or less, you do not lose any Wounds."
"The armour gains +1 AP for each Rune of Stone. Suits with one or more Runes of Stone, and no other runes, are exempt from the Rule of Pride."
"When you suffer a Critical Wound whilst wearing this armour, you may Reverse the roll on the Critical Wound table."

"The armour loses the Weakpoints Flaw, can never be Damaged except by a Runic Flaw, and never reduces its AP due to Talents or effects such as the Penetrating Quality. Effects that ignore armour and inflict Wounds directly still apply."
"Whilst wearing this armour, you can only suffer a maximum of 10 Wounds from any instance when Damage is inflicted."

"When the talisman is pressed to your eye, you negate any penalties imposed by fog, mist, smoke, or other clouding, non-magical vapours. Two Runes also penetrate magical vapours. Three Runes allow you to see clearly even in total darkness."

"The talisman glows brightly if pressed into contact with an item that has been faked, forged, counterfeited, or deliberately degraded in value. Two Runes also identify magical illusions or duplicates. Three Runes reveal the precise method of deception to the bearer."

"When the talisman is pressed to the user's eye, their vision is magnified, allowing them to clearly see events up to a mile away. Two Runes extend vision up to two miles. Three Runes extend vision up to four miles."

"Whilst wearing this talisman, you can never acquire the Ablaze Condition, are immune to heat exposure, and reduce all incoming Damage from fire and flaming attacks by 4 for each Rune of the Furnace."

"Whilst wearing this talisman, you gain 1 Fortune point for each Rune of Luck, which can exceed your usual maximum Fortune. You lose these Fortune points when you remove the talisman (to a minimum of 0 Fortune), and cannot regain them until the following session."
"After a good night's sleep whilst wearing this talisman, the bearer regains their Toughness Bonus in Wounds for each Rune of Restoration."

"Whilst wearing this talisman, and using the Magic Resistance Talent, you can activate a Rune of Spellbreaking to automatically count as rolling 01 on your Willpower Test. You can activate each Rune of Spellbreaking once per adventure, and must choose to activate it before you roll."

"If you successfully dispel a spell using the Magic Resistance Talent whilst wearing this talisman, the spellcaster cannot attempt the spell again for your Willpower Bonus in Rounds. Two Runes extend this effect to your Willpower Bonus in hours. Three Runes extend it to your Willpower Bonus in weeks."
"Whilst wearing this talisman, you may impose a -10 penalty for each Rune of Warding on attack Tests or spellcasting Tests targeting you."

"Whilst wearing this talisman, if an enemy within line of sight casts a spell, you may either Reverse their Spellcasting Test, or Reverse your Opposed Willpower Test (if you're in range to attempt Magic Resistance)."
"Whilst wearing this talisman, you may take an extra Endeavour between adventures."
"Whilst wearing this talisman, you may Reverse any Charm, Intimidate, and Leadership Tests you make that target a Dwarf, or a group mostly consisting of Dwarfs."

"Whilst wearing this talisman, and Moving no faster than walking pace, you can Move through solid, immobile objects like trees, rock, and metal cages. You cannot Move through animals or Undead creatures. You cannot end your Move inside a solid object."
"Whenever you take Damage from a Melee attack, the attacker immediately suffers 2d10 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points as normal."

"The runic item emits a loud, blaring noise if any creature of Size Small or larger enters its range of effect. Two Runes may instead bellow a pre-recorded sentence. Three Runes may instead transmit a pre-recorded telepathic message to the crafter or their closest living descendant, over any distance."
"Affected allies begin combat with 1 Advantage for each Rune of Battle."
"Affected allies gain +10 on Psychology Tests for each Rune of Courage."

"For each Rune of Discovery the runic item has, the crafter may choose a specific metal or gem (e.g. gold, diamond, gromril, iron ore, obsinite, ithilmar, brightstone). The runic item glows brightly if the specified material appears within its range of effect."

"For each rune, describe a type of creature: a general creature type (Skaven, obvious Chaos worshippers), or a more specific description. When a creature that clearly matches the description enters the range of effect, the rune glows a violent crimson."

"Any locks within the runic item's range of effect are immune to being picked or forced except by magic or the corresponding key. Two Runes also protect from magical effects. Three Runes are proof against the lock's corresponding key: only the crafter, or their closest living descendant, can open the lock at will. A lock may still be bypassed by smashing through the chest or door they protect."
"Affected allies gain +20 for each Rune of Purification on Tests to resist toxins in air and water."

"If a creature violates the sanctity of dead bodies within the runic item's range of effect (e.g. stealing from the dead, casting a necromantic spell), they immediately gain 1 Ablaze Condition for each Rune of Retribution."
"Affected allies gain +10 for each Rune of Sanctuary on Willpower Tests to dispel with Magic Resistance."
"Enemies attempting to Engage an affected ally reduce the distance they can Run by 4 yards for each Rune of Slowness, to a minimum of the enemy's Walk distance."

"Rodents, Skaven, and rat-based abominations like Rat Ogres lose 2 Wounds for each Rune of Verminkill (ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points) when they enter the runic item's range of effect, or start their Turn within it."

"Affected allies may Reverse any Test to resist corrupting influences, Tests to avoid mutation from Corruption, and rolls on the Physical and Mental Corruption Tables. In addition, when an affected ally is engaged with a Daemonic enemy that has the Unstable Trait, they count as having +2 Advantage when calculating Wounds lost for being Unstable."
"You may Reverse enemy Ranged attack Tests made against affected allies."
"You may Reverse any enemy spellcasting Tests made against affected allies."
"Affected allies begin combat with 1 Advantage. Double the range of this rune's effects to 12 yards, or 24 yards if forged upon a battle standard."

"Affected allies may Reverse any Willpower Test to Oppose spellcasting with Magic Resistance. The range limit for Magic Resistance is removed: affected allies can Oppose any spell cast against a target in their line of sight, and the Talent can be used to dispel persistent spells, not just incoming spells."
"When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to hit for each Rune of Accuracy."
"A target struck by this weapon gains 1 Ablaze Condition per Rune of Burning."
"When you Fumble and/or Misfire whilst using this weapon, the crew may activate this rune to negate the effects. You can activate each Rune of Forging once per adventure."
"The weapon inflicts +2 Damage for each Rune of Penetrating."

"The weapon reduces its Reload Rating by 2 for each Rune of Reloading. If this would reduce the Rating to 0 or below, the weapon loses the Reload Flaw. Weapons with the Salvo Quality cannot be reduced below Reload Rating 1."
"When this weapon attacks a flying enemy, you gain +20 to hit for each Rune of Seeking."
"Dwarfs crewing this weapon begin combat with 1 Advantage for each Rune of the Stalwart. This extra Advantage is lost by any Characters that leave the weapon's crew, or become Engaged in melee."
"Dwarfs gain +10 Willpower for each Rune of the Valiant whilst crewing this weapon."
"The weapon's crew always count as being in hard cover, imposing a -30 modifier on Ranged attacks against them."

"The weapon is invisible to all enemies until it fires, at which point it becomes visible for the rest of the combat. The weapon's crew remain visible as normal, and moving the machine still causes noise."

"Any Dwarf crewing this weapon may choose to activate the rune as a Free Action, triggering the machine's self-destruction. All creatures within 6 yards of the machine take 15 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Survivors gain the Ablaze Condition. The weapon itself is destroyed."

"When making a Ranged attack with the weapon, you may activate this rune to count as rolling 01. If the attack succeeds, it also counts as a Critical, and may strike any location you choose. You may activate this rune once per adventure, and must decide to activate it before you roll."

"Doom Rune (Anvil of Doom, activated as an Action, Hard (-20) Runesmithing Test). The blessing of Valaya: all Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom may count as rolling 01 on any Cool Tests they make until the end of the next Round."

"Doom Rune (Anvil of Doom, activated as an Action, Hard (-20) Runesmithing Test). The blessing of Grungni: all Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom improve the AP of any armour they're wearing by 2, until the end of the next Round."

"Doom Rune (Anvil of Doom, activated as an Action, Hard (-20) Runesmithing Test). The blessing of Grimnir: all enemies within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom are struck for 12 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points."
